# .cursor/ Directory — Distro Code Managed

## The Golden Rule

> **NEVER install MCPs, plugins, skills, rules, extensions, or any tooling via the Cursor Settings UI, `cursor --install-extension`, the command palette, or any manual method.**

This is not a suggestion. This is a hard requirement.

### Why

Cursor's settings interface is **unstable, opinionated, and designed to lock you in**:

- **No visibility.** The UI gives you no clear picture of what's installed, what's conflicting, what version you're on, or what's silently failing. You can't diff it, review it, or audit it.
- **No reproducibility.** User-level installs go to `~/.cursor/` which is invisible to teammates, not version-controlled, and impossible to debug when something breaks on one machine but not another.
- **Constant churn.** Cursor's settings UI changes frequently. Options move, rename, or disappear between versions. Anything configured through it is fragile.
- **Duplicates and collisions.** Installing an MCP server through the UI while the extension is managing the same server at the project level creates duplicates in the MCP panel — same server appears twice, configs conflict silently.

**Everything must be in the code.** Configuration lives in `.cursor/config-repo/` (committed, code-reviewed) or `.cursor/config-user/` (gitignored staging area). All tooling is transparent, diffable, and decoupled from Cursor's UI.

---

## What the Distro Code Extension Does

The [Distro Code](https://github.com/distro-ai/dc) extension manages MCP servers, hooks, rules, skills, commands, and settings. It injects them into this repo on every Cursor activation. You do not need to install anything manually.

### Exactly what files and folders are written

The extension writes to **these specific paths and nowhere else**:

| Path                               | What happens                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.cursor/config-universal/`        | **Wiped and recreated** from the extension bundle every activation              |
| `.cursor/config-user/`             | **Scaffolded** (subdirs + seed files created if missing, never overwritten)     |
| `.cursor/rules/`                   | **Managed files replaced** via three-tier merge (manually-placed files survive) |
| `.cursor/skills/`                  | **Managed directories replaced** via three-tier merge                           |
| `.cursor/commands/`                | **Managed files replaced** via three-tier merge                                 |
| `.cursor/agents/`                  | **Managed files replaced** via three-tier merge (manually-placed files survive) |
| `.cursor/mcp.json`                 | **Rebuilt** from three-tier JSON merge                                          |
| `.cursor/hooks.json`               | **Rebuilt** from three-tier JSON merge                                          |
| `.cursor/settings.json`            | **Rebuilt** from three-tier JSON merge                                          |
| `.cursor/rules/mcp-first.mdc`      | **Auto-generated** MCP routing rule                                             |
| `.cursor/.universal-injected.json` | **Manifest** tracking what was injected                                         |
| `.cursor/README.md`                | **This file** — overwritten from extension bundle                               |
| `.vscode/extensions.json`          | **Rebuilt** from DC bundle + config-repo merge                                  |
| `.git/info/exclude`                | **DC section appended** (gitignore patterns for generated files)                |

### What the extension does NOT touch

- **`~/.cursor/`** — nothing is read, written, or deleted at the home directory level. Zero.
- **`.cursor/config-repo/`** — committed to git, team-managed. The extension never writes here.
- **`.cursor/BUGBOT.md`** — team-managed, committed directly.
- **`.greptile/`** — team-managed, committed directly.
- **`.cursorindexingignore`** — team-managed (DC sections stripped as one-time cleanup on first activation only).
- **`.claudeignore`** — team-managed (DC sections stripped as one-time cleanup on first activation only).
- **Hook script files** — stay in their tier folders (`config-universal/hooks/`, `config-repo/hooks/`, `config-user/hooks/`). Never copied elsewhere.
- **Custom MCP server `.js` files** — stay in their tier folders. Never copied elsewhere.
- **Any file outside `.cursor/`, `.vscode/`, and `.git/info/exclude`** — the extension does not touch your source code, configs, or anything else.

## Three-Tier Configuration System

| Tier               | Location                    | Visibility                     | Who manages    | Conflict behavior                              |
| ------------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Tier 1 (Universal) | `.cursor/config-universal/` | Gitignored (extension-managed) | DC maintainers | Always wins                                    |
| Tier 2 (Repo)      | `.cursor/config-repo/`      | Checked into git               | Team via PR    | Overwritten by Tier 1 on conflicts             |
| Tier 3 (User)      | `.cursor/config-user/`      | Gitignored                     | Individual dev | Additive only; collisions dropped with warning |

### Merge order

1. Start with EMPTY config
2. Apply Tier 2 (config-repo) entries
3. Apply Tier 1 (config-universal) entries — overwrites any Tier 2 conflicts
4. Apply Tier 3 (config-user) entries — additive only, collisions dropped with warning toast
5. Write output file / directory

Output files are entirely derived. Editing them directly does nothing — they get overwritten.

### Files copied (three-tier directory merge)

| Asset    | Extension               | Output              | Cleanup                                                                                |
| -------- | ----------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rules    | `.mdc`                  | `.cursor/rules/`    | Manifest-based (only previously-injected files deleted; manually-placed files survive) |
| Skills   | subdirs with `SKILL.md` | `.cursor/skills/`   | Manifest-based                                                                         |
| Commands | `.md`                   | `.cursor/commands/` | Manifest-based                                                                         |
| Agents   | `.md`                   | `.cursor/agents/`   | Manifest-based (only previously-injected files deleted; manually-placed files survive) |

### JSON merged (no files move)

| Asset       | Output                    | Path rewriting                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| MCP servers | `.cursor/mcp.json`        | `./` paths rewritten to full tier path    |
| Hooks       | `.cursor/hooks.json`      | `./hooks/` rewritten to full tier path    |
| Settings    | `.cursor/settings.json`   | Tier 3 additive only (collisions dropped) |
| Extensions  | `.vscode/extensions.json` | DC bundle + config-repo merge             |

### Path rewriting

When hooks.json and mcp.json entries are merged from tier folders, relative paths (`./`) are rewritten so they resolve correctly from the workspace root:

| Path in tier config                               | What gets written to merged output                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `"./hooks/my-hook.sh"` in config-repo             | `".cursor/config-repo/hooks/my-hook.sh"`             |
| `"./custom-mcp-servers/server.js"` in config-user | `".cursor/config-user/custom-mcp-servers/server.js"` |
| `"/usr/local/bin/something"` (absolute)           | `"/usr/local/bin/something"` (unchanged)             |
| `"npx"` (bare command)                            | `"npx"` (unchanged)                                  |

## What Goes in `.cursor/config-repo/`

These files are checked into git and code-reviewed:

| File / Directory          | Purpose                                           |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `mcp.json`                | Team MCP servers (`{ "mcpServers": { ... } }`)    |
| `hooks.json`              | Team hooks (`{ "version": 1, "hooks": { ... } }`) |
| `hooks/*.sh`              | Hook script files referenced by hooks.json        |
| `rules/*.mdc`             | Team Cursor rules                                 |
| `skills/*/`               | Team skills (each with a `SKILL.md`)              |
| `commands/*.md`           | Team slash commands                               |
| `agents/*.md`             | Team Cursor IDE subagents                         |
| `custom-mcp-servers/*.js` | Team custom MCP server files                      |
| `settings.json`           | Team Cursor settings                              |
| `extensions.json`         | VS Code extension recommendations                 |

### Example: adding a repo-specific MCP server

Edit `.cursor/config-repo/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "my-team-server": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "my-mcp-package@latest"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Example: adding a repo-specific hook

Create `.cursor/config-repo/hooks/my-hook.sh` and edit `.cursor/config-repo/hooks.json`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "hooks": {
    "on_file_save": [{ "command": "./hooks/my-hook.sh" }]
  }
}
```

The `./hooks/` prefix is rewritten during merge to `.cursor/config-repo/hooks/my-hook.sh`.

### Example: adding a repo-specific agent

Create `.cursor/config-repo/agents/my-agent.md`:

```markdown
---
name: my-agent
description: Use when doing X. Specializes in Y.
---

You are a specialist in Y. When invoked...
```

## What Goes in `.cursor/config-user/`

Gitignored. Scaffolded automatically. Edit `.cursor/config-user/mcp.json` to add a personal MCP server — the extension picks it up immediately via file watcher.

Same structure as config-repo. **Additive only** — collisions with Tier 1 or Tier 2 are dropped with a warning toast.

**This is a staging area, not a personal customization layer.** Maximum 72-hour experimentation window — if it's valuable, promote to `.cursor/config-repo/` via PR.

---

## Cold Start / Fresh Clone

After `git clone`, only `.cursor/config-repo/`, `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`, `.greptile/`, and this README exist. Everything else is created automatically when Cursor opens with the DC extension installed (~2s).

## Troubleshooting

### The manifest: `.cursor/.universal-injected.json`

This file is your first stop for diagnosing injection issues. It's a complete snapshot of the last injection/rebuild. Open it and check:

| Field                | What it tells you                                                                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`            | Extension version that wrote this manifest                                        |
| `injectedAt`         | When the extension last ran a full activation                                     |
| `lastRebuiltAt`      | When the last merge happened (activation or file watcher)                         |
| `lastRebuildTrigger` | What caused the last rebuild (`activation`, `watcher:mcp`, `watcher:rules`, etc.) |
| `rules`              | Full list of rule files in `.cursor/rules/` that the extension manages            |
| `skills`             | Full list of skill directories in `.cursor/skills/` that the extension manages    |
| `commands`           | Full list of command files in `.cursor/commands/` that the extension manages      |
| `agents`             | Full list of agent files in `.cursor/agents/` that the extension manages          |
| `hooks`              | Full list of rewritten hook command paths in the merged `hooks.json`              |
| `mcpServers`         | Full list of ALL MCP server names in the merged `mcp.json` (all tiers)            |
| `settingsKeys`       | Keys present in the merged `settings.json`                                        |
| `readme`             | Path of the injected README file                                                  |
| `outputHashes`       | MD5 content hashes of each generated output file at time of write                 |

### Common diagnosis steps

**"My MCP server isn't showing up"**

1. Check `mcpServers` in the manifest — is it listed?
2. If not, check your tier config file (`.cursor/config-repo/mcp.json` or `config-user/mcp.json`)
3. Check `lastRebuiltAt` — has the extension run since you made the change?
4. Check `lastRebuildTrigger` — if it says `activation` but you just edited config-repo, the watcher may not have fired

**"Something changed my output file after I edited it"**

1. Check `lastRebuiltAt` — the extension re-merges on every activation and on file watcher events
2. Output files are ALWAYS overwritten. Edit the tier source file, not the output.

**"Did the last rebuild actually change anything?"**

Compare the stored hash against the current file:

```bash
# What the manifest recorded
cat .cursor/.universal-injected.json | grep -A1 'mcp.json'

# What's on disk now
md5 -q .cursor/mcp.json        # macOS
md5sum .cursor/mcp.json         # Linux
```

If the hashes match, the file hasn't changed since the extension wrote it. If they differ, something modified the file after the extension (e.g., Cursor's UI, another extension, or a manual edit).

**"Is the extension even running?"**

Check `injectedAt` — if it's hours/days old, the extension may not be activating. Reopen Cursor or check the DC output channel (`View > Output > Distro Code`).

**"I see duplicate MCP servers in Cursor's panel"**

The extension warns on activation if user-level configs exist in `~/.cursor/`. Check the warning toast. Remove user-level MCP servers from `~/.cursor/mcp.json` — all MCP config belongs in the project-level tier system.

## Known Limitations

| Scenario                             | What happens                                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Extension not installed              | No MCP servers, hooks, rules, or skills. Install via dev setup script.     |
| Fresh clone before first activation  | Generated output files do not exist. Extension recreates everything (~2s). |
| User-config lost after re-clone      | Gitignored, so it's gone. By design — promote to config-repo if valuable.  |
| User edits output file directly      | Overwritten on next activation.                                            |
| Tier 2 key same name as Tier 1       | DC silently overwrites the config-repo entry.                              |
| Tier 3 key collides with Tier 1 or 2 | Dropped with warning toast.                                                |
| Malformed JSON in config             | Skipped, other tiers proceed. Check DC output channel.                     |

- `.cursor/mcp.json`
- `.cursor/hooks.json`
- `.cursor/settings.json`
- `.cursor/rules/` (managed files)
- `.cursor/skills/` (managed directories)

- `.cursor/rules/mcp-first.mdc`
- `.cursor/config-universal/`
- `.cursor/.universal-injected.json`
- `.cursor/README.md` (this file)
- `.vscode/extensions.json`
